subject: Lynx.ai side-by-side performance proof and tiered commitment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@lynx.ai>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: priya@lynx.ai, procurement@lynx.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask — side-by-side perf numbers before renewal

Rachel —

Appreciate the demo last week. Leadership is asking for a head-to-head run with our incumbent before we sign off on the renewal. They want: a 2-week side-by-side on our workload (chat + embeddings), P95 latency at 512 tokens, and cost per 1M tokens comparison. Procurement also needs basic SSO/KMS checklist.

We want to understand if Redwood can guarantee sustained 5k rps at target latency and whether your caching/batching will actually reduce tokens in production. Can you do this by EOW (we need results to present in the 12/21 exec review)?

Thanks,
Samir
VP Engineering, Lynx.ai

[Attachment: lynx_eval_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet) — sample queries & traffic mix]
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@lynx.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask — side-by-side perf numbers before renewal

Samir —

We can run a controlled side-by-side. Short answer: yes.

Proposal in brief: 2-week dedicated proof using a reserved Redwood Dedicated pool with a pinned model variant, mirrored traffic from your csv (thanks for the matrix). We'll run our standard KV/prefix caching, an ops-controlled batching policy, and a quantized float16 path so the cost comparison is apples-to-apples. Deliverables: daily P95/P99 latencies, throughput (rps), token counts, and a cost model.

To proceed we need: a small account-level firewall allowlist, temporary service account for ingestion, and a procurement email to sign an SOW for a short test. Timeline wise, if we kick on Thursday (12/17), we can hand you an interim report on 12/20 and final on 12/30 — does that meet your exec timing?

I'll loop in Marissa for pricing and Ben for ops.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: internal — Lynx side-by-side ask (prep checklist)

Folks —

Notes from my side: we should offer a two-tier commitment if they sign a 12-mo post-proof contract: 1) Pilot-only: 2-week proof at $X/day on Dedicated (no commitment), 2) Commit tier: 12-mo minimum commit that buys ~20% unit discount and guaranteed capacity uplift window. Procurement will want a short SOW + confidentiality clause and an SLA-lite for the proof.

Operational checklist:
- Runbook: redwood_sidebyside_runbook.pdf (I’ll draft)
- Snapshot metrics dashboard with token breakouts
- Ops run: enable prefix caching + 8-shard batching profile by default
- Clear abort/fallback policy to hosted API to avoid blackouts

Ben — can you confirm if we can reserve one 8-GPU pool for 12/17-12/30 and give me a quick cost delta? Karthik — pricing input for tiered term sheet (I’ll attach a stub).

Marissa
Director, Solutions
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: internal — Lynx side-by-side ask (prep checklist)

Marissa/Rachel —

We can carve an 8-GPU pool 12/17–12/30. Cost uplift for the reserved test is $7,500 for the period (run + infra). Ops notes: we’ll default to the KV cache and a dynamic batching window tuned for 5–15ms latency budget. If they push sustained 5k rps we’ll need a short warm-up of 2 hours to populate caches.

I’ll prepare the runbook and dashboard link. Also recommend we enable request-level tracing for the first 48 hours (helps debug regressions).

Ben
Sr. Infra Ops
From: Priya Rao <priya@lynx.ai>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@lynx.ai>, procurement@lynx.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up — procurement / SSO / KMS 

Rachel —

Procurement here. Quick checklist items for the proof:
- SSO integration (SAML) to the trial console
- KMS integration for keys used during the proof (we need your HSM/KMS partner details)
- Evidence for SOC2 scope (summary) for procurement review
- Confirmation you will not retain request payloads beyond the proof period (we prefer 30 days deletion window)

Can you send a short SOW and an export of the SOC2 posture? We can turn quickly on the SOW if terms look standard.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Procurement, Lynx.ai
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Priya Rao <priya@lynx.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@lynx.ai>, procurement@lynx.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Side-by-side run scope, SOW link, and tiered term commitment offer

Priya/Samir —

Thanks for the checklist — attached is a short SOW (DocuSign link below) that covers the 2-week proof window and the post-proof tiered commitment options. Highlights:
- Proof scope: 12/17–12/30, dedicated 8-GPU pool, mirrored traffic using your matrix.
- Deliverables: daily latency/throughput reports, token accounting, and a final cost comparison report.
- Security: SAML SSO to the trial console, KMS integrations supported (we work with AWS KMS, Google KMS, and partner HSMs); we will not persist request payloads beyond 30 days for this trial. SOC2 summary attached.
- Commercial: Pilot fee $7,500 (covers reserved infra & ops); post-proof 12-mo commit tier gets 20% off unit price and a guaranteed 10% capacity uplift SLA window (subject to standard terms).

DocuSign SOW: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/LYX-4592-term-sheet
Drive folder (runbook + dashboard): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-lynx-sidebyside

Attachments: redwood_sidebyside_runbook.pdf, tiered-pricing-term-sheet.pdf, SOC2-snapshot.pdf

If this works, procurement can route the SOW and we’ll start the run on 12/17 as planned. If execs still need an interim 12/20 note, I’ll provide a mid-proof status update with P95 and token delta.

—Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_sidebyside_runbook.pdf (pdf)]
